name: West Virginia
$scopeNote: WIRED TO CALC-CODE (2026-08-21, follow-up pass): originally a DATA-ONLY pass (Scott: 'do the Dakotas and the Virginias, just for the data'), left unwired deliberately. Built out once Scott asked to close PA reciprocity's open items. West Virginia's real structure: a 5-bracket progressive percentage-method table (2.11%-4.58%) with a genuinely unusual TWO-TABLE selection mechanic (not marital-status-driven), a 5-state reciprocity cluster (the largest in this project), and flat per-week municipal 'City Service Fees' in several cities -- a structurally different local-tax shape from every other local tax modelled so far (a flat dollar amount, not a percentage of wages). IMPORTANT DIFFERENCE FROM VIRGINIA: WV's own IT-100.2A publishes genuine, independently-set PER-PERIOD tables (weekly/biweekly/semimonthly/monthly/daily/annual, all 6, times both earner tables = 12 full tables) rather than one annual formula meant to be divided -- re-fetched and fully transcribed all 12 this pass (closing a previously-disclosed gap outright, not approximating around it) rather than deriving per-period figures from the annual table the way this engine does for VA/DC/NJ/DE, since a spot check showed WV's own period boundaries do NOT cleanly divide from the annual ones (e.g. annual $7,500 / 52 = $144.23, but the source's own weekly table boundary is $144 flat -- a small but real independently-set figure, not a rounding of the annual one).

sources.title: WV State Tax Division -- Withholding Help and General Information page, "Supplemental Wages" guidance
sources.verifiedBy: Fetched directly for the 'find and fix anything missing across all 50 states' pass. The page describes a MARGINAL-AMOUNT method: annualize standard (regular) pay to get a base annual figure and its tax, separately annualize standard pay plus the bonus and get its tax, and withhold the difference — its own worked example: a biweekly $2,000 earner ($52,000 standard annual) receiving a $5,000 bonus withholds the bonus at 4.82%. Attempted to wire this via the existing aggregateWithPriorRegularPayment() mechanism (combine this cheque's bonus with a caller-supplied prior regular payment, tax the combined PERIOD total through the ordinary two-table formula, subtract tax already withheld on the regular portion) — but WV's own IT-100.2A tables are published PER-PERIOD with no annual table at all (this file's own withholdingStructure.brackets.$comment already establishes that), so combining $2,000 + $5,000 = $7,000 and running it through the BIWEEKLY table is a PERIOD-level aggregate, not the ANNUAL-level marginal calculation the help page's own prose describes. Testing this against the page's own $2,000/$5,000 example produced 4.58%, not the stated 4.82% — a real, unresolved discrepancy, not a rounding artifact of the kind already documented for California's Examples E/F. NOT wired this pass rather than shipped unverified; see knownGaps.

withholdingStructure.mechanism: Subtract a flat per-period dollar amount PER EXEMPTION CLAIMED (WV/IT-104's own count: 1 for self if claimed, up to 2 for married if not claimed elsewhere, plus 1 per dependent) from gross wages, then look up the result in one of TWO 5-bracket progressive tables -- selection is NOT based on marital status directly, but on an employee ELECTION (IT-104 Line 5): the 'Two Earner/Two or More Jobs' table applies by DEFAULT (i.e. whenever Line 5 is unchecked, regardless of actual marital status), and has LOWER bracket thresholds (withholds MORE); checking Line 5 (available only to Single/HoH/married-with-nonemployed-spouse employees on ONE job) switches to the 'Optional One Earner/One Job' table, which has thresholds exactly 4/3 (=1.3333...) times the two-earner table's at every tier and withholds LESS. This selection mechanic -- an employee opt-IN to a lower-withholding table, defaulting to the higher one -- is structurally different from every other state built in this project (all of which select a table by declared filing status, not by an earner-count election).
withholdingStructure.exemptionAmountNote: Identical across BOTH the two-earner and one-earner tables -- only the bracket thresholds/bases differ, not the per-exemption subtraction.

brackets.$comment: All 12 tables (6 periods x 2 earner types) transcribed directly from IT-100.2A (March 2026 revision, re-fetched 2026-08-21) -- these are the source's OWN independently-published per-period tables, not derived from the annual one. Dispatch (westVirginiaWithholding() in src/taxes/state.ts) looks up the table matching input.payFrequency directly; no annualize-then-divide step exists for WV.
brackets.note: Both tables' per-period boundaries are INDEPENDENTLY published, not derived from the annual figure -- verified this pass by direct comparison: annual $7,500/52 = $144.23, but the source's own weekly boundary is $144 flat (a real, if small, divergence). Every cell above transcribed directly from the re-fetched March 2026 PDF, not scaled from the annual table -- closes this file's own previously-disclosed 'not cell-by-cell verified' gap outright rather than accepting the risk.

withholdingStructure.noCertificateDefault: WV/IT-104's own instructions don't state an explicit no-form default the way Kansas's KW-100 or Delaware's regulation text do; by this project's standing convention, absent a certificate the safer assumption is 0 exemptions and the higher-withholding two-earner table (not independently confirmed against a WV-specific statement this pass -- flagged as inferred, not sourced).

reciprocity.mechanism: Form WV/IT-104NR (the reverse side of IT-104), filed by the employee with the employer.
reciprocity.rule: A resident of Kentucky, Maryland, Ohio, Pennsylvania, or Virginia whose ONLY West Virginia-source income is wages/salary is fully exempt from WV withholding -- confirmed by direct quote from IT-104NR's own text: 'you are exempt from West Virginia Personal Income Tax Withholding.' Also covers military spouses under the Military Spouses Residency Relief Act via the same form.
reciprocity.confidence: primary_source_confirmed -- read directly off the actual certificate form, the strongest sourcing tier this project uses for a reciprocity claim (same tier as Ohio's IT 4NR, Kansas's KW-100 worked example). This is the LARGEST reciprocity cluster of any state in this project so far (5 states, vs. Wisconsin's/Michigan's/Ohio's 4-6 but WV's is unusual for a Mid-Atlantic-adjacent state) -- notably RECIPROCAL WITH VIRGINIA, which should be cross-checked against Virginia's OWN reciprocity list when VA is built (a natural consistency check, same pattern as this project's WI/MI/IL/IN five-state cross-check).

outOfStateConstructionRate.note: 1% surtax on top of the 8.5% base for out-of-state construction employers, per secondary sourcing.

unemploymentInsurance.confidence: cross_source_confirmed only -- workforcewv.org's own page gates the actual rate table behind an authenticated employer system, not a public static page; a direct fetch attempt confirmed this rather than assuming it. Wage base and new-employer rate are consistent across every secondary source checked with zero dissent.

localIncomeTax.rule: NOT a percentage-of-wages tax the way every other local tax in this project is (PA Act 32 EIT, OH municipal tax, MI city tax, Newark's payroll tax) -- West Virginia's local levy is a flat FEE PER PAY PERIOD, structurally closer to a fixed toll than an income tax. Cities (Charleston $2.50/wk, Huntington $5/wk, Morgantown $3/wk, Parkersburg $2.50/wk, Wheeling $2.00/wk, Weirton $5.00/wk) impose a mandatory 'City Service Fee' or 'Municipal Service Fee' under WV Code 8-13-13, withheld by the employer from any employee whose DUTY STATION is in that city (i.e. work-location-based like Newark's, not residence-based).

cityDetail.parkersburgTwoFeesNote: RESOLVED an apparent conflict found this pass ('fix any and all gaps'): Parkersburg's own fees page (fetched directly) confirms $2.50/wk is the CITY SERVICE FEE specifically ('a flat charge of $2.50 per week for individuals who work at a job within the city limits,' employer-withheld, remitted quarterly) -- a SEPARATE, unrelated levy from Parkersburg's own Police Protection Fee ($8/mo residential, $16/mo commercial properties), which is a property-based charge, not a payroll withholding. Not a contradiction; two different fees that a naive comparison could have conflated.
cityDetail.wheeling: $2.00/week, confirmed directly (Bloomberg Tax + Wheeling's own DWC Help Desk summary): applies to full-time, part-time, and self-employed individuals who regularly report to work (including remote work FROM a Wheeling location) within city limits, residents and nonresidents alike. A 30-consecutive-day-in-the-city threshold applies before the fee attaches, and an employee working multiple jobs in Wheeling is only assessed once. Effective 2020-01-01.
cityDetail.weirton: $5.00/week as of a 2026 rate INCREASE, confirmed via a direct fetch of local news coverage of the city council's own April 14, 2026 vote (Ordinance 2272, 6-1) -- up from $2.00/week (unchanged since the fee's original 2004 enactment). Effective 30 days after the council vote (~2026-05-14), per the ordinance's own stated implementation timeline. Same multi-job-deduplication rule as Wheeling's. This is a REAL mid-2026 rate change, the same class of watch-item as Ohio's HB96 mid-year cut -- a check date before ~2026-05-14 should arguably still use $2.00/week, though this file only carries the current/final $5.00 figure since STALE, corrected: WV local municipal service fees ARE wired -- westVirginiaMunicipalServiceFee() in src/taxes/state.ts, gated on certificate.locality (verified: Wheeling produces a $2.00/week WV_LOCAL_FEE line).

localIncomeTax.confidence: cross_source_confirmed across multiple secondary payroll-industry sources with consistent figures for all 6 cities; Charleston's own official fee-overview document exists but was only linked, not independently read as inline text. Parkersburg's fee page and Weirton's rate-increase news coverage WERE fetched and read directly this pass. NOT an exhaustive list of every WV municipality with a service fee -- 9 of an unknown total were captured as of 2026-08-31 (Fairmont, Madison, and Romney added this session with primary-ordinance sourcing, up from 6), the same disclosed-partial-coverage convention this project used for Ohio's initial 3-city local pass before the full 679-municipality bulk load. No statewide aggregator was found for this fee (each city sets and administers its own, confirmed by a dedicated search this pass finding no centralized list). RETRIED 2026-08-31 with real internet access, still could not expand the list: (1) WV Code 8-13-13's own text (fetched directly, code.wvlegislature.gov) is a general home-rule grant to any municipality furnishing an 'essential or special municipal service' -- it names no cities and creates no registry, confirming this is structurally unlistable from the statute. (2) WV Municipal League's site (wvml.org) was fetched directly and has no member directory page or fee list. (3) Of WV's next 5 largest cities after the current 6 (Fairmont, Beckley, Martinsburg, Clarksburg, South Charleston), only Fairmont's site was reachable at all -- Beckley and Clarksburg were rejected by this environment's own network egress policy, Martinsburg returned a bot-block 403, and South Charleston's TLS connection failed outright -- and Fairmont's homepage has no fee-related link or mention, which is weak evidence of absence, not confirmation (a fee could exist on an unlinked sub-page). Closing this out as still-open: getting a true statewide count needs either a bulk records request to the WV State Auditor/Municipal Home Rule Board or a city-by-city pass across all ~230 incorporated municipalities, not a homepage-level web search. FOLLOW-UP 2026-08-31 SAME DAY, with WebSearch instead of blind crawling: found a much better lead -- a USDA National Finance Center bulletin references “Nine West Virginia cities require employees who work there to pay a local city service fee: Charleston, Fairmont, Huntington, Madison, Montgomery, Morgantown, Parkersburg, Weirton, and Wheeling.” Fairmont and Madison were confirmed via their own primary ordinance PDFs and added to serviceFeeCities above. Montgomery is real (Municode indexes its own “CHAPTER 6 - CITY SERVICE CHARGES FOR POLICE AND FIRE PROTECTION,” and EY Tax News has two dated alerts on it: a 2019 alert titled ‘imposes new city service fee to be withheld from wages’ and a 2020 alert on a further increase) but its CURRENT dollar rate could not be pinned down this pass -- Montgomery’s own city site (montgomery.wv.gov) has no fee page reachable from its homepage, Municode serves Montgomery’s code as a JS shell like every other Municode instance already documented in this project, and the EY alerts are paywalled. Deliberately NOT added to serviceFeeCities with a guessed number. This NFC-sourced 9-city list is very likely still not exhaustive either (it is scoped to cities relevant to federal payroll, not a general WV registry), but it is the best lead found so far for closing this out completely. SECOND FOLLOW-UP 2026-08-31, same session, user asked to close WV out entirely: a WV Municipal League-sourced list (surfaced via a Clarksburg search) named a DIFFERENT 9 cities -- Fairmont, Charleston, Huntington, Romney, Parkersburg, Wheeling, Morgantown, Weirton, and Chester -- overlapping the NFC list on 7 but adding two more real leads. Romney: CONFIRMED and ADDED ($1.00/week, nonresident-only, same shape as Fairmont) -- see serviceFeeCities.Romney above for the full ordinance citation. Chester: real (a 2023 local news article confirms Chester city council actively administers a municipal fee), but every source found describes an ANNUAL, PROPERTY-billed fee with late-fee/lien mechanics, not a per-week PAYROLL-withheld one like every other city on this list -- genuinely unclear whether Chester's fee is even the same WV Code 8-13-13 payroll mechanism this file models, so deliberately NOT added rather than guessed into the wrong shape. Also broadly WebSearched (not just site-crawled) for the fee at WV's next tier of cities by size -- Beckley, Clarksburg, Martinsburg, South Charleston, Bridgeport, Elkins, Buckhannon, Grafton, Princeton, Bluefield, Moundsville, St. Albans, Vienna, Point Pleasant -- and found nothing tying any of them to a per-employee service fee; Bridgeport has its own '$100/year or $8.33/month Service Fee' but every source describing it calls it a UTILITY fee, structurally different from the payroll withholding this file models, so also not added. This is meaningfully stronger evidence of absence than the first pass's site-crawl (a broad web search surfaces news coverage and industry guides, not just each city's own homepage), but it is still evidence of absence from search results, not a canvassed 'no' from all ~230 municipalities -- a WVU shared-services page (wvusharedservices.wvu.edu/s/article/City-User-Fee) that likely has WVU's own authoritative multi-city list for exactly this purpose could not be reached (blocked by this environment's egress policy on that specific domain), which is the most promising remaining lead if this gets picked up again.
localIncomeTax.knownGap: WIRED (2026-08-24 pass, right after Denver's OPT): westVirginiaMunicipalServiceFee() in src/taxes/state.ts, gated on certificate.locality the same way Newark's/Denver's/Missouri's local taxes are. Genuinely new calc-code shape as this note originally said (flat per-week fee, not a wage percentage) -- NOT a reuse of Newark's percentage mechanism. Per-period conversion (weeklyRate x 52 / periodsPerYear, rounded down like PA's LST) is an INFERRED convention, not verbatim from any of the 6 cities' own sources, since none of them state a per-pay-period breakdown -- disclosed as an assumption, not confirmed. Still NOT modelled: Weirton's mid-2026 rate change has no effective-dating mechanism (same class of gap Ohio's HB96 had before midYearEffectiveDating existed -- this file only carries the current $5.00 figure, correct for any check date on/after ~2026-05-14 and WRONG for one before it); Wheeling's 30-consecutive-day threshold before the fee attaches (this engine has no employment-duration input, so every duty-station-in-Wheeling case is treated as already past the threshold); and the multi-job dedup rule (same class of un-modelled multi-employer coordination as Newark's TD269-style cases elsewhere in this project).

Fairmont.$addedNote: ADDED 2026-08-31: confirmed directly from the City of Fairmont's own Ordinance No. 1812 (fetched and parsed as a primary PDF, not a secondary summary), which states verbatim: 'there is hereby imposed, established and charged upon each non-resident employee employed within the corporate limits of the City of Fairmont by an employer, a special charge of two and 00/100 dollars ($2.00) per week.' This is explicitly a NON-RESIDENT charge withheld via payroll -- Fairmont residents instead pay an $8.67/month fee billed directly (not payroll-withheld), per a secondary source that surfaced this ordinance. WIRED: westVirginiaMunicipalServiceFee() reads nonResidentOnly and skips the fee when certificate.residenceCity also names Fairmont, so a resident is not incorrectly charged through payroll.

Madison.$addedNote: ADDED 2026-08-31: confirmed directly from the City of Madison's own City Service Fee Ordinance PDF (madisonwv.org), fetched and parsed as a primary source. Verbatim: 'Beginning January 1, 2020 and continuing thereafter, the fee rate imposed shall be $3.00 per calendar week of employment within the city' (up from $1.25/week which applied 2017-2019). Applies to 'each employee and self employed individual... of employment within the city' -- no residency qualifier in the ordinance text, unlike Fairmont, so treated as work-location-based like Wheeling/Weirton.

Romney.$addedNote: ADDED 2026-08-31 (same follow-up session, second pass): found via the WV Municipal League's own city list (surfaced through a Clarksburg search), then confirmed directly from the ordinance text itself (published as a legal notice on wvlegals.com, cross-checked against a WV Dept of Revenue Home Rule Program amendment filing dated 2026-01-07). Verbatim: 'There is hereby imposed an annual city service fee upon each employer, employee and self-employed individual at the rate of One Dollar ($1.00) per calendar week of employment within the City,' with Section 5 explicitly excluding 'Residents of the City of Romney... who resides at a property that concurrently pays the City user fee' -- the same nonresident-only structure as Fairmont, so nonResidentOnly:true here too. Called an 'annual' fee in the ordinance's own title despite being assessed and collected weekly/quarterly like every other WV city's fee -- a naming quirk of this specific ordinance, not a different mechanism.

paidLeave.rule: NONE for the private sector. West Virginia has no state-funded mandatory or voluntary Paid Family/Medical Leave program for private employers. SB 114 (2026 Regular Session) created only a narrow 2-year Paid Parental Leave PILOT PROGRAM for STATE EMPLOYEES (up to 12 weeks, birth/adoption/foster placement of a child under 12) -- out of scope for a general private-sector payroll engine, the same convention this project uses for public-employee-only programs.

exemptPretaxComment: RESOLVED this pass (was previously an open item with no array value at all, which broke the engine outright the moment WV got wired to calc-code -- ctx.taxableWagesFor() requires an array). Confirmed via W. Va. Code R. sec. 110-21-12 and secondary corroboration: West Virginia adjusted gross income of a resident individual starts from 'federal adjusted gross income... with certain modifications' -- same FAGI-conformity structure as Virginia. 401(k)/125/HSA/etc. deferrals are already excluded from FAGI at the point of measurement, and no modification found adds them back. Same confidence tier as Virginia's (this pass) and Indiana's/Kentucky's list-read confirmation.
knownGaps: WIRED to calc-code this pass (westVirginiaWithholding() in src/taxes/state.ts, method west_virginia_dual_table). Dispatches directly off input.payFrequency using the genuine per-period tables (no annualize/divide step) -- proven via 2 hand-derived tests in tests/engine.test.ts, describe('West Virginia'), one per earner-table.
Per-period bracket tables are now FULLY transcribed and wired (all 6 periods x 2 tables) -- this specific gap is closed, not just re-disclosed.

The 5% mid-year rate cut's own narrative (retroactive effective date, bill number) is cross-source only, not confirmed against tax.wv.gov's own 'Personal Income Tax Reduction Bill' page or bill text directly -- though the RATE TABLE itself (IT-100.2A) is primary-sourced and dated March 2026.

City Service Fee coverage is now a 6-city sample (Charleston/Huntington/Morgantown/Parkersburg/Wheeling/Weirton, up from 4 this pass), still not an exhaustive statewide enumeration of every WV municipality with WV Code 8-13-13 authority -- Ohio-style bulk-load-from-a-state-aggregator was not attempted because a dedicated search this pass confirmed no equivalent statewide aggregator exists for WV's fee (each city sets and administers its own). PARKERSBURG NOW PRIMARY-CONFIRMED (this pass): the city's own finance-department fees page states the City Service User Fee is 'a flat charge of $2.50 per week for individuals who work at a job within the city limits', withheld by the employer and remitted quarterly — matching the figure already on file. That same page is also the reason to be careful expanding this list: Parkersburg separately levies a POLICE PROTECTION fee ($8/month residential, $16/month commercial), a fire fee by square footage, and a sanitation fee, none of which are payroll deductions. A WV city having 'a fee' does not make it an employee fee, so each addition needs the ordinance read rather than a fee schedule skimmed.
UI rate/wage-base figures are cross-source only -- workforcewv.org gates the actual current rate table behind an authenticated system, confirmed by direct fetch attempt rather than assumed.
exemptPretax RESOLVED (see exemptPretaxComment above) -- WV conforms to federal AGI, confirmed via W. Va. Code R. sec. 110-21-12.
No-certificate default (0 exemptions, two-earner table) is this project's standing convention applied by analogy, not confirmed against an explicit WV instruction the way Delaware's or Kansas's was.

The marginal-amount supplemental method requires the caller to supply input.priorRegularPayment (this period's or the employee's standard regular taxable wages, and what WV tax would be withheld on that alone) -- without it, a standalone bonus cheque falls back to this engine's existing default (annualize the bonus alone through the ordinary two-table formula), the same disclosed approximation every other state without a caller-supplied prior payment already carries in this project.

Supplemental wages: WV's own Withholding Help page describes a real, distinct marginal-amount method for bonuses (see this file's own sources[] entry, "Supplemental Wages" guidance) -- but reproducing it exactly against the page's own $2,000-regular/$5,000-bonus worked example (stated answer: 4.82%) was NOT achieved this pass: combining the two amounts through this engine's existing period-level aggregation mechanism (aggregateWithPriorRegularPayment) yields 4.58%, because WV's own IT-100.2A tables are per-period with no annual table, while the help page's prose describes annualizing first. Left UNWIRED rather than shipped with an unverified number -- a standalone bonus falls back to this engine's existing default (the ordinary per-period formula on the bonus alone). Flagged for a dedicated follow-up pass that resolves the annual-vs-period mismatch, not silently guessed at. WIRED, WITH A DISCLOSED DISCREPANCY (perfect-parity pass): westVirginiaSupplementalAnnualMarginal() in src/taxes/state.ts now implements the annual-marginal method against IT-100.2A's own published ANNUAL bracket table (brackets.*.annual -- this file's earlier claim that no annual table exists was itself wrong; it's present, just not what was checked at the time). Run against the help page's own $2,000-regular/$5,000-bonus example, this produces $229.00 (4.58%, IT-100.2A's own top marginal rate) rather than the page's stated 4.82%. Every bracket-grounded interpretation tried this pass (annual table, biweekly period-level combine, both earner-type table variants) converges to 4.56%-4.58%, never 4.82% -- the working theory is a typo in the help page's own prose, not an error here, but that theory was NOT confirmed against a second WV source. Shipped anyway because 4.58% is directly traceable to IT-100.2A's own published rate and strictly improves on the prior fallback (the ordinary per-period formula on the bonus alone, which doesn't annualize at all). See the function's own doc comment and tests/engine.test.ts for the full disclosure.

The detailed unemploymentInsurance block above stays the record of research; this exists because that block's shape varies too much between states to compute from directly (wage bases as objects, industry-keyed rate maps, differently-named keys).

suiEmployer.newEmployerRateSource: This state's own unemploymentInsurance block above, researched in an earlier pass — kept in preference to any aggregate table.

US DOL's 'Significant Provisions of State UI Laws, Effective January 2026' comparison table (oui.doleta.gov/unemploy/content/sigpros/2020-2029/January2026.pdf) states 1.50%-7.50%.
